entries.proposition: Design: saline, ethosuximide and levetiracetam in a counterbalanced within-animal sequence with at least 6 days between treatments, blinded analysis, in transgenic and wild-type littermates, so spike classes present in both genotypes can be compared by genotype and drug.
entries.snippet: The washout period between treatments was at least 6 days for each animal. The order of drugs was counterbalanced, and the person conducting the recording and analysis was blinded to the treatment.

entries.proposition: Genotype-restricted phenomena exist only for rare spike classes: spike-wave discharges, cortico-hippocampal spikes with afterhyperpolarisation and giant spikes were seen almost exclusively in the transgenic mice and only in a subset of them, while the common classes did not differ by genotype.
entries.snippet: Cortical spikes were slightly more common in APP/PS1 mice (p = 0.045), while SWDs (p = 0.04), CH spikes with after hyperpolarization (p = 0.02) and giant spikes (p = 0.008) were detected almost exclusively in APP/PS1 mice, but only in a subset of them as seen from large error bars in Figure 11.
entries.anchor: Results, Only SWDs, CH-Spikes With After Hyperpolarization and Giant Spikes Were Clearly Overrepresented in APP/PS1 Mice

entries.proposition: Ethosuximide effects on classes present in both genotypes track each other: the authors write that, in as much as spikes were present in wild-type mice, their response to the drugs seemed to follow the pattern of the transgenic mice; the spike-wave discharges, the one absence-type class, did not respond to ethosuximide in either genotype.
entries.snippet: In as much as spikes were present in wild-type mice, their response to AEDs seemed to follow the pattern of APP/PS1 mice (Figure 11).
entries.anchor: Results, The Spike Types Differ in Their Response to Ethosuximide and Levetiracetam

entries.proposition: Spike-wave discharges did not respond to either drug in the whole sample or in either genotype alone (statistics F(2, 6) = 2.0, p = 0.21 for the pooled sample, with wild type p = 0.70 and transgenic p = 0.22), on very few animals.
entries.snippet: SWDs did not respond to AED treatment [All: F(2, 6) = 2.0, p = 0.21; WT: F(2, 4) = 0.4, p = 0.70; TG: F(2, 6) = 2.0, p = 0.22].
entries.anchor: Results, The Spike Types Differ in Their Response to Ethosuximide and Levetiracetam

entries.proposition: Statistical limit stated by the authors: heterogeneity between individual animals was high (counts consistent between two saline sessions within an animal) and so a two-way ANOVA could not be applied; per-genotype one-way tests with 3 to 6 degrees of freedom were used. No treatment-by-genotype test exists in the paper.
entries.snippet: Due to the high inter-individual variability in the spike occurrence, we could not apply a two-way ANOVA model.
entries.anchor: Results, The Spike Types Differ in Their Response to Ethosuximide and Levetiracetam

entries.proposition: Figure 11 read as an image: panel B (cortico-hippocampal spikes) falls with ethosuximide in both wild type (black, about 19 to about 5 per hour) and transgenic (red, about 22 to about 6); panel C (spindle-associated spikes) rises in both; panel F (fast-spindle spikes) falls in both; panel D (spike-wave discharges) shows a transgenic subset at about 400 per hour on saline and no clear fall on ethosuximide; panel H (giant spikes) shows transgenic only with stars for levetiracetam and not ethosuximide.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 11B: black WT dots about 19 on saline, about 5 on Esm; red TG dots about 22 on saline, about 6 on Esm; Figure 11D: single TG outliers near 400 and 570 per hour.
